newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche BA changes fare, route structure.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche BA changes fare, route structure.

text.p: Deutsche BA said it will drop its domestic business class, simplify prices and add new routes from January 20.
The German airline, in which British Airways holds a 49 percent stake, said the changes would offer passengers improved services at attractive prices.
Deutsche BA will launch eight flights a day on its new routes between Munich-Hamburg and Munich-Cologne, a company statement said.
In the new single class, snacks only will be served after 08:45 but breakfast will still be served on early-morning flights, the airline added.
Deutsche BA will also introduce new standard return prices for all domestic German destinations with three types of ticket.

A super-value ticket for bookings 14 days in advance will cost 190 marks, a value ticket for seven days in advance will cost 290 marks and a flexi-ticket with full re-booking options will cost 520 marks.
The prices for the new Munich-Hamburg route will be slightly higher, the airline said.
Deutsche BA chief commerical officer, Paul Giblin, said: "We want to offer our clients the friendly, reliable and inexpensive service which they expect from us."
The airline said it would outline the changes fully at a news conference on January 20.
